acceptanceCriteria: tests validity on a committed Jest/Vitest spec file emits one tests[] entry per example, in the RSpec path's output shape
Run-state facts: it.skip, xit, it.todo, it.only/fit, describe.skip, and test.each row binding are reported; skipped/todo/focused examples are INELIGIBLE as the RSpec equivalents are
Example facts: an example with no assertion (following helpers the reader can resolve) is flagged; expectations only on constants or tautologies are flagged

Stub facts: jest.mock/jest.spyOn/vi.mock of the module or class under test is distinguished from boundary modules (HTTP clients, fetch, timers); strength stays NOT_MEASURED with these facts as its reason
Reading is confined to the committed blob at --rev and abstains when the spec blob differs from the receipt's, as the RSpec path does
Unparseable or unsupported JS/TS shapes abstain rather than claim; TSA spec amended with new requirement IDs; focused testsource/testvalidity/testvaliditydoc/cmd tests pass
body: GitHub #1159. `corvint tests validity --files <x.spec.ts> --rev <sha>` returns tests: [] for Jest/Vitest files, while RSpec examples get per-example hygiene (V1-1798, TSA-V0-062..072: skipped/pending/focused, shared-only, no-expectation, described-class stub). A pipeline gating citations on tests validity can only abstain for JS/TS. The V1-1798 build log lists 'JS/TS discovery attaching source findings' as a residual. Ask: the same output shape for JS/TS, reusing the tests lint JS/TS reader.
title: GH #1159: per-example test-validity hygiene for Jest/Vitest examples (tests validity returns no tests for TS/JS files)
